items.description: 🔥 Join Maker School & get customer #1 guaranteed: https://skool.com/makerschool/about 💎 Get all course resources 100% free: https://skool.com/maker-zero/about ➡️ If this is your first video: I'm Nick Saraev. I run LeftClick, an AI growth agency. We've done work for large brands you're likely familiar with, like Mr. Beast, Anthropic, OpenAI, and a few others. In plain English: I help people build systems that generate leads, close deals, and scale businesses, mostly using new AI models like Claude. I also make videos about how to do all of that here on YouTube. It hasn't always been this way. My family immigrated from a Soviet bloc country (People's Republic of Bulgaria) in the 90s. They worked extremely hard, and we were broke for a very long time. I grew up wishing for more security, stability, and freedom over my own life. I don't have a programming degree, and never took formal education for IT or workflows. I learned it all myself from YouTube videos like you're watching now. As for my path: I started my first business at 19 in college. We threw events (mostly parties) at campus bars, and charged people for entry. That failed to provide me enough money to pay my bills, so at 21, I started another business, a door-to-door marketing agency. From there, every year, I would start several companies, over 10 in total. I did this in a variety of industries, like e-commerce, photography, videography, SaaS, credit repair, etc. Each grew slightly more profitable, until, at 25, I would start 1SecondCopy, a content writing company. A friend and I eventually scaled that to over $90,000/m. It was my first taste of financial independence, and the reason I'm here today. Since starting my journey, I've grown a fair bit of capital. To diversify my income, at 30, I began investing in other businesses and advising companies on how to grow in the AI era. These include SaaS businesses, like Clairvo, agencies like Dental Connect, and more. Collectively, the businesses that I own outright or are a part of generate over $10 million per year. This returns far more than the 5-10% you would get in the stock market, but also requires a lot of my active time. There's a tradeoff there, but I greatly prefer active investing, where I have control over the entities I'm a part of. It wasn't easy to get here. But I did in the end! For anyone on their own entrepreneurial journey: I wish you luck, happiness, and perseverance. You can make it! Summary ⤵️ Here are some practical tips on Claude Code that I've learned after spending $31,141 and over 1,000 hours working with AI models. You'll learn how to make your outputs more reliable through evals and self-checks, minimize wasted context, run parallel work in defined scopes, and more. Chapters: 0:00 I've spent over $30,000 on Claude Code 0:29 You can't trust the first output 3:19 A way to check their own work 4:38 Let the code be the context 6:38 Letting Claude write your prompt 8:11 Watch what is eating your context window 10:11 Loosening the leash 11:54 Diagnosing before you start a fix 13:01 MCP servers 14:56 Run scoped tasks in parallel 16:50 Always start fresh with a handoff note 17:52 Ask side questions with /btw 19:01 Fan out and fan in 20:53 Set up your CLAUDE.md 22:17 Keep a backup tool ready 23:52 Have Claude learn from its mistakes 25:21 Maker School

items.title: Reading Code Beats Writing It
items.description: Which matters more now, writing code or reading it? Reading, by a mile. When AI generates this much code, the bottleneck stops being how fast you type and becomes how fast you can review. That's why fluency with Git, pull requests, navigating a codebase, and moving through commits is what levels you up. A senior engineer with those skills plus AI tools ships multiples of what was possible a few years ago, which is exactly why senior demand is growing while routine coding shrinks. The leverage has moved to the people who understand the system. #techwithtim #softwareengineering #techjobs

items.description: Secure your MCP server using Descope for free: https://www.descope.com/ MCP servers are quickly becoming one of the most important pieces of the AI ecosystem. We’ll cover what MCP is, how local and remote servers differ, how access control works, and how the MCP protocol connects AI models to external tools and data. Then we’ll put it all together by building an MCP server and adding authentication so you can see how these systems work in practice. items.description: Try Mira for free 👉 https://t.me/mira?start=aitrendz The next AI era is not about tools. It's about directing AI agents from a single chat. Mira lets you do exactly that inside Telegram. No complicated setups or jumping between tools. Just one chat. You can set up recurring tasks like Bitcoin price alerts or daily news updates, access multiple LLMs, image, video, and music models all in one place, and even add Mira into your team group chats to collaborate. Use skills for repetitive workflows and let it handle the heavy lifting. Instead of doing everything yourself with AI, you tell Mira your goal and it figures things out on its own. This is where I believe we're heading. It's on Telegram now and coming to iMessage and Slack soon! Try it for free and comment your favorite use case below. Follow me for more AI breakdowns. #Mira #AIAgents #AITutorial #Telegram #AIAgent

items.title: Building AI Assistants with On-Device Memory
items.description: Learn More: https://bit.ly/4AlVW2n A cloud-based assistant can remember what it sees, hears, and is told, but only by staying connected and sending that data to a remote server. In our new short course, Building AI Assistants with On-Device Memory, built in partnership with Qdrant and taught by Dylan Couzon, Developer Experience Engineer at Qdrant, you'll learn to store and search an assistant's memories locally, so nothing has to leave the device. In this course, you'll learn how to: - Build a local memory system that stores, retrieves, filters, and forgets text and image memories. - Build an offline assistant that recalls experiences across text, voice, and images. - Teach an AI application to recognize new objects from stored examples without retraining a model. - Run the on-device AI assistant on a local machine, including Mac, Windows, and Linux. This course also includes our new AI coding lab, so you can practice building with an AI coding agent from the DeepLearning.AI mobile app. Enroll Now:https://bit.ly/4AlVW2n

items.title: Full Course: Spec-Driven Development with Coding Agents
items.description: Vibe coding is fast, but it often produces code that doesn't match what you asked for. Spec-driven development is the disciplined alternative: write a clear markdown spec defining what to build, and let your coding agent implement it. Earn your certificate here: https://bit.ly/4hmJc2K You'll learn to: - Write a project constitution defining mission, tech stack, and roadmap - Plan, implement, and validate features using a spec as the agent's guide - Introduce SDD to a legacy codebase - Package your workflow into an agent skill that's portable across agents and IDEs Spec-Driven Development with Coding Agents is built in partnership with JetBrains and taught by Paul Everitt, Developer Advocate at JetBrains. Recommended: basic familiarity with a programming language and experience with LLM-based coding tools.
